proof_review.finding: Expansion of parabolic cosets into maximal-parabolic cosets is valid; repeated types collapse because intersecting cosets coincide. Product identity and complements have the corrected union.

Cartesian coset decomposition after common B-normalization proves flag transitivity; marker supports and orbit intersections determine every flag stabilizer. All three cases of residue generation are proved. Thinness, chamber freeness and full group follow.

v1 proof wrongly presumed generated-support parabolics contained the chamber kernel. v2 uses intersections C_E of image maximal parabolics, which all contain H; images in the faithful quotient are generated complementary supports. The twisting parabolics are full preimages, including H⋊B for a transitive orbit.

The explicit reduction assumes B flag-transitive. Then its normal chamber kernel acts trivially on X and on the Coxeter group, so it is contained in every twisting parabolic. Full-group claims stay with faithful models. An arbitrary non-flag-transitive representation is not claimed covered.

Generator definitions are independent of transporters by the stabilizer relations. Inverse-paired double cosets enumerate unordered pair orbits. Opposite homomorphisms prove the full group presentation, including fixed vertices.
Projection to B forces even exponents and rank-two Coxeter subgroups give exact inner pair order, including infinite order.
Leaf removal preserves the possible exceptional edge; Boolean diagonal group attaches an exact label4 edge. One- and two-node bases and recursive group order are provided.

All retained and copied edges, all omitted edges, singleton orbit conditions, and the mixed2m label agree with the source. Both six-vertex example diagrams are recovered; text/picture discrepancy is disclosed.

Marked presentations and parabolics give the stated isomorphisms relative to the explicitly retained book descriptions. The book was not newly fully read; no independent derivation of the original classical construction is claimed.
